title: Injecting a Custom UVM Phase
description: Insert a firmware-loading phase into the UVM schedule and verify it executes between reset and configure.

steps.title: Step 1: Complete the Singleton
steps.instructions: Open `testbench.sv` and complete the `load_fw_phase_c` singleton: declare `m_inst` and implement `get()` so every call returns the same phase object (the phase IMP). The constructor is `protected`, as in uvm-core's built-in phases, so only `get()` can create it.

steps.title: Step 2: Connect the Phase to the Environment
steps.instructions: Override `exec_task(uvm_component comp, uvm_phase phase)` in `load_fw_phase_c`: `$cast` `comp` to `soc_env` and call `env.load_fw_phase(phase)`. Then implement `soc_env::load_fw_phase`: raise an objection, check `reset_done`, print `uvm_info("ORDER", "load_fw", UVM_LOW)`, wait 20ns, set `firmware_loaded`, increment `fw_loads`, and drop the objection. Without `exec_task`, the phase runs but never calls your code.

steps.title: Step 3: Insert Into the Schedule and Run
steps.instructions: In `base_test::build_phase`, call `uvm_domain::get_uvm_schedule().add(load_fw_phase_c::get(), .after_phase(uvm_reset_phase::get()))` once (`get_uvm_schedule()` is a uvm-core implementation call); `reset_phase` lives in the uvm run-time schedule, not the common domain. Run and check the log: `[ORDER] reset` at 0, `load_fw` at 50, `configure` at 70 and `main` at 80 ns, with no `ORDER` errors. Add `+UVM_PHASE_TRACE` to see each phase start and end.

steps.title: Step 4: Break It and Predict
steps.instructions: Starting from your working solution, predict each log before you run it, then confirm it (README, "Break it and predict"): (a) delete `exec_task`: `configure` at 50 ns with the ORDER errors, and the trace shows `load_fw` skipped; (b) call `add()` on `uvm_domain::get_common_domain()`: `UVM_FATAL [PH_BAD_ADD] cannot find after_phase 'reset' within node 'common'` during build; (c) add `.before_phase(uvm_configure_phase::get())`: the same ORDER times, but the trace shows `post_reset` starting at 50 ns beside `load_fw` (a parallel branch); (d) remove the `phase_registered` guard and register twice: `load_fw` at 50 and 70 ns, `configure` at 90 ns, and `Firmware loaded 2 times`.

steps.title: Step 5: Try the Existing Phase Instead
steps.instructions: Remove the phase registration and move the body of `load_fw_phase` into a `post_reset_phase` task in `soc_env`. Predict, then confirm, that the log shows `reset` at 0, `load_fw` at 50 and `configure` at 70 ns, the same order with no change to the shared schedule. Write one sentence on when a team would still add a custom phase.
